newsitem.title: GERMANY: EVA Air to expand Europe freight capacity.
newsitem.headline: EVA Air to expand Europe freight capacity.

text.p: Taiwanese airline Eva Air said it will launch a major expansion of European services from May 8 with new flights to Amsterdam and Brussels.
The airline will fly three times a week to Amsterdam from Taipei via Dubai with McDonnell Douglas MD-11 passenger aircraft, a company statement issued here said.
The flights will be able to carry up to 275 passengers and 15 tonnes of cargo, it added.
The existing three times a week MD-11 freighter service from Taipei via Singapore and Dubai to Amsterdam will be split with Brussels.
The MD-11 aircraft, with freight capacity of up to 80 tonnes, will operate weekly to Amsterdam and twice-weekly to Brussels, with a road trucking network covering central Europe.

K.T. Chiu, EVA Air senior vice-president public relations, said: "Our cargo services from Amsterdam have been extremely successful, achieving load factors of around 90 percent, but we recognise also that Schipol is a key international gateway and transit hub for passengers."
The transfer of two freighter services to Brussels would allow it to offer passenger services from Taiwan to the Netherlands for the first time, he added.

EVA Air Germany sales manager Pei-Fang Wagner forecast the additional freight capacity would allow the airline to increase its current ex-Germany tonnage of 350 tonnes a month. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
